notes:
Mazda SkyActiv cars: the Mazda3, Mazda6, CX-5 and CX-9 that opendbc lists and the Mazda 2, Mazda 3, CX-3, CX-30, CX-5, CX-50, CX-60 and MX-5 that OBDb has repositories for, read over the OBD-II socket's 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s with UDS service 22.

Every row is an address pair and nothing more: no data identifier or scaling is shipped, because the only sources are other projects' signal definitions, which this repository does not copy. Each row cites every archived OBDb repository that lists its pair. The units answer the standard identification and fault-code reads once `obd-read probe` shows them present. OBDb gives no unit type for any address except the engine, transmission and CX-60 motor, so most rows are named by address. opendbc names four of the addresses (steering 0x730, ABS 0x760, forward radar 0x764 and forward camera 0x706) from the firmware queries comma.ai's driver-assistance software sends to those units.

Where the two sources differ: OBDb has rows for 0x730 and 0x760 and none for 0x764 or 0x706, so the radar and camera rest on opendbc alone, with the reply identifier inferred as request plus 8. Some OBDb pairs break the plus-8 pattern: 0x7D0 replies from 0x7DA, and the Mazda 2's 0x600, 0x620 and 0x621 reply from 0x680, 0x6A0 and 0x6A1. OBDb's CX-50 lists 0x7D2 with the same reply identifier 0x7DA as 0x7D0, which a profile cannot carry twice, so 0x7D2 is left out. OBDb sends to 0x750 with the extended address 0x2A first and does not say which address byte its replies start with; the adapter layer accepts only replies that start with the tester address 0xF1, as for the BMW units, which for this unit is an inference. Several rows rest on one repository (0x600, 0x620 and 0x621 on the Mazda 2, 0x725 and 0x747 on the CX-50, 0x775 and the 0x7E3 motor on the CX-60, 0x7E6 on the CX-30), and the CX-3 file lists only the engine, transmission and 0x720. Mazda's body modules sit partly on a slower bus (MS-CAN) that a plain adapter on the OBD-II socket may not reach, so some rows may stay silent. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows it answering. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened.
